annotations.text:
BROADSHEET — chosen 2026-09-16.
Sidebar revealed (⌘⇧S), terminal | browser split, ⌘K open. The 30px top strip keeps identity and window controls when the sidebar is hidden.
Spaces are windows: the Space row at the top of the sidebar is a window switcher (⌘⌥1–9); the tab list is this Space only.
Wordmark: Newsreader Italic. UI face and terminal face are both config keys (default IBM Plex Mono).

CHROMELESS — the default. Full-bleed terminal, a 4px hot edge where the sidebar hides. The localhost hook is a ruled chip anchored to the detected line (⌘↵ split, ⌘⇧↵ new tab). Attention state surfaces in the top strip, not as a popup.
QUICK TERMINAL — ⌥⌘T drops a sheet from the top edge over whatever is focused (here a browser tab in the blue 'work' Space). Same 2px edge + hard shadow as the palette.
PIP — our own always-on-top window drawing a tab's texture: a video (left) or a terminal tab you're keeping an eye on (right). Signal band shows which Space it came from; ↗ returns it to its tab.

TOKENS — what spike 4 renders from: paper/ink for both themes, six Space signals, ANSI 0–15 per theme, type ramp (IBM Plex Mono + Instrument Serif wordmark), rule weights, spacing, states, keys, principles.
Direction pass, kept for the record. Broadsheet was chosen; Aurora and Instrument are not being built.

SIDEBAR — third pass. Hover the left edge to reveal; hides ~300 ms after the mouse leaves; Ctrl+Shift+S pins.
Space row = window switcher. Pinned row. Compact rows (number · kind glyph · title · cwd/host); the 52px preview expands only under the hovered row (03) and under a waiting tab (02).
Footer: Space avatar + name + browser identity, shell profile row, assistant router row, + new tab / settings.

SETTINGS TAB — Ctrl+, opens a native tab. Sections left; key / control rows right (ruled segmented switches, boxed fields). Every change writes ~/.config/nus/init.luau, shown live at the bottom; the file stays the source of truth.
